result.reason: Section 11.4 substantively reaches the preferred position: Corio may terminate on 30 days' written notice without an early-termination charge, receives a refund of prepaid fees attributable to the post-termination period, and Commerce One has no convenience-termination right during a committed term. However, the redline unnecessarily adds the extensive Section 11.3, which creates unrelated survival, support, payment, use, and confidentiality obligations and therefore does not preserve unrelated commercial intent. Drafting is generally workable, but “in whole or in part” is broader and less precise than necessary, and Section 11.3 contains drafting defects such as “it's” instead of “its” and poor punctuation around “provided, however.”
